additional_info.subject: RE: ID0369856-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / R6 170002125] Sitop going in overload error CRM:00579000961
additional_info.body:
Hello Marnic,
Greetings of the day!
We received your query-
Sitop power supply keeps going in overload error sometimes also
when charger is turned off (QA2 not).
As you said, Charger works fine when you
reset the overload error. Kindly confirm, here resetting the error means
are you rebooting the charger?
Refer the diagram below (highlighted part):
We need to check all the wirings and connections corresponding to TB17 for any loose connections.
Kindly check all the fuses from FC12 to FC17, whether they are blinking green or not.
To check if there is any fault due to fuses, check by turning off each fuse one at a time, if we are getting the overload error.
If everything works well, then need to check the Sitop (TB17) itself, if its faulty. You can check the same by replacing/exchanging it from the other charger.
If TB17 found to be faulty or broken, then needs to replace it.
We will wait for your feedback to proceed further.
Thank you
Best Regards
eMobility Tech Support Team - Vaishnavi Raut

Br.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0369856-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / R6 170002125] Sitop going in overload error CRM:00579000983
additional_info.body:
Dear
Regarding to the Sitop, we changed the Sitop power supply, and the problem seems to be solved for now. On the other hand, the charger was stuck during the startup on 8 or sometimes 42%. We did a cfast flash and this solved the problem. Charger is booting now without any problems only an new error on the LEM appeard, “tampering”.
We restarted the charger and LEM many times but the error keeps appearing. We did not touched or manipulated the LEM so we think the device is broken. Please give permission to change DC2 LEM.
Br.
